content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an algorithm for learning disentangled representations (more precisely, group-structured representations of pairs of points in the data space) to achieve better compositional generalization. The key assumption is that the data is generated by a free and faithful group action. Two models are learned: an encoder from a pair of elements to the latent group element relating them and a "decoder" that models the group action. Experiments on dSprites and 3D Shapes datasets show favorable performance in reconstruction of images with attribute combinations not seen in training compared with VAE-based methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- (++) Motivation. Compositional generalization and structured latent representations are an important direction and the intro + related work introduce the context well.
- (+) Presentation. I could not find any bugs in the math and the uses of group theory concepts and notation are appropriate.

Weaknesses / questions:
- (--) The latent group is assumed to be the additive group of $\mathbb{R}^n$. (By the way, this is not stated in the text, but can be deduced from the code.) This is obviously a strong limitation.
  - Could the proposed approach be generalized to more interesting groups? For instance, many problems require invariant/equivariant representations w.r.t. Lie groups, such as $SO(n)$. (It seems like the math would be the same, but it would be good to see discussion and an experiment on this, even in a simple case like a torus $SO(2)^n$.)
  - This work is very similar in spirit to [Keurti et al., arXiv:2207.12067], in which an encoder and decoder to a latent space is learned along with a model mapping a **known** group element relating two datapoints to its action on the latent space, via the Lie group exponential map. Could you comment on the similarities and differences with such an approach?
- (--) There is no theoretical result about the proposed algorithm, yet the setup is begging for an identifiability theorem. (For example, is it true that the globally optimal encoder from pairs or images to the latent group recovers the true mapping up to conjugation by a group automorphism?)
- (-) It looks like what was done is more like a simple autoencoder, not a variational AE. Would it make more sense to compare with low-dimensional AE approaches and not VAE ones?
  - I disagree with the first sentence of section 4, since VAE encoders specifically aim to approximate the uncertainty in the posterior over latents, negating the one-to-oneness of the mapping from the latent space to the data manifold. Could the sentence be qualified with some details -- is it that the strong constraint of unimodality on the encoder and decoder implicitly makes this assumption?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: good, see above.

Quality, novelty: The contribution is limited by the small experiments and the rigid assumptions made in them, as well as the lack of theoretical analysis.

Reproducibility: Good; code is provided. (The code does contain many files and pieces that are not essential, and I would have found a pruned, illustrative example more helpful.)
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper suggests a promising approach for learning group-structured relative representations of pairs of points in the data space, but experiments with more interesting group actions and supporting theory are  important missing pieces in the current version of the paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a novel approach for image generation that simulates the group structure and the group action. This is done by inputting a pair of data to the encoder for it to learn the difference between the two data, and giving the decoder not only the output of encoder, but also one of the data in the data pair. The authors claim that by this means and with the proposed loss, the decoder can learn to decode the transformation from the input data to the output data.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
I do not work in this field, so I will provide my opinions based on my understanding of this paper.
As I understood, the novelty of the proposed method lies in using paired data as input, as well as feeding the decoder with the image data, so that the model can understand the difference between the input data pair. Based on the reconstruction error, this model can work better than VAE. 

However, even with little experience in this area, I doubt the novelty of the proposed method. This type of difference modeling seems ad hoc. I think there should be related work that has already explored this direction using similar approaches.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
I believe the clarity of this paper if mediocre since I find it hard to fully understand the proposed approach. 

I cannot assess the novelty of this paper since I have no related experience.

I believe the paper contains enough information for reproduction.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work proposes a novel framework to generate data and robustly generalize to data with distribution shifts.  The argument of this paper is that the group action with all three axioms improve combinatorial generalization capacity and model the transformation properties. The experiments show that the proposed method (i.e., MAGA) is superior compared to past models (e.g., vanilla VAE, beta VAE, and factor VAE) on several benchmark e.g., dSprites and 3D shapeswith two settings: Recombination-to-Element, and Recombination-to-Range.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The motivation is clear that the proposed method targets to beat combinatorial generalization in previous works  e,g., distangled representations.
- The use of group and group action and VAE for combinatorial generalization is somewhat novel and under explored in past work with similar themes.
- The performance is quite strong compared to some prior works (e.g., $\beta$ VAE and factor-VAE) based on the BCE reconstruction error.

Weaknesses: 
- Even though the motivation for combinatorial generalization is clear but the motivation for distribution shifts is vague. There is no sufficient background described in introduction why the distribution shift is a main concern here and what the past models have achieved to tackle this problem.
- In Section 1, there is no fact that explains about the failure cases in prior works  addressing the problem of combinatorial generalization for out-of-distribution data or distributions shifts. Either mathematical proofs, empirical proofs, or previous cited works need to explain about this phenomenon and how deteriorating the impacts are. The nuance of this work is to combine two different problems under the same umbrella but it is lacking of supported evidences to prove these two problems do exist and interrelate.
- Figure 1 is not descriptive and informative as it does not expose the differences between the normal VAE and MAGA. “The encoder encodes the difference between two data” is not depicted in Fig. 1, also the decoder decodes the transformation from the input data is not sketched in Fig. 1. For instance, the figure can be improved with two parts in the latent z to show differences. The figure needs an update to clearly show the difference MAGA and VAE in a more fundamental level matching the figure description. 
- In Section 4, “Previous unsupervised representation learning methods tend to consider that the latent space has a one-to-one correspondence to the data space. ” Please give the readers more informatoin about these methods and citations to them.
- In Section 4, there is no definition of factors and how it relates to the characteristics in the training data. This work is encouraged to cite some works that have discussed about this concept e.g., Kim et al., “Disentangling by Factorising ”, Locatello et al., “Disentangling Factors of Variation using Few Labels”.
- In Section 4.1, there is no detailed description about $x_1$ and $x_2$ but the work directly uses them for the proposed losses.
- Why is the input for the decoder $x \in X$? As understood, the decoder generates the image based on the latent input. However, the equation is written as $D(., x_i)$.
- Comparison to recent works is crucial. The methods for comparison is outdated and not representing the recent work. It is suggested to include some more recent work in the tables for comparison e.g., Yang et al. (2021) and Locatelo et al. (2020). 
- The methods for comparison are not explained in detail in the experimental section. It is not very clear what is beta VAE, factor VAE with different values for the coefficients.
- There are some grammatical errors:
    - “supposed to finds”, “a approaches”, “the methods showed” (there is only one method proposed in this paper)
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is not very clear especially in terms of motivation, main problems, past works/citations, and some definitions. The quality of writing needs some improvement also as there are some grammatical errors and unclear meanings/messages in text.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper has some potentials to show the contribution of the group and group action concept to model transformation. However, the issues in this paper are: unclear target problems in the first two sections, non-rigorous experiments without comparing with some recent SOTAs, some missing citations and definitions. Considering all these issues and strengths, the recommended score is "reject".

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper propose a new VAE framework to  model the transformation between data. The proposed method has better performance than vanilla VAE-based methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Weakness
* Designing of MAGA network is not properly evaluated. There are many potential choice of pivot-based VAE structure. (1) Why x1 and x2 are concatenated before encoder. Is it a better way to concatenate encoded feature vector? (2) Is the skip conntection (fed x1 to decoder) effective? What will happen if we do not fed x1 to decoder. (3) Otherwise, what will happen if we do not fed x1 to encoder but only decoder?
* Meanwhile, CONCAT two images together and adopt a convolution network not seems a great choice to model difference context. A potential better choice is to extract feature of two image separately (with shared weight) and then use a module (such as Transformer) to model long-distance relation information.
* Authors should also evaluated VAE-based methods with pair image inputs.
* I do not agree that the evaluation results with different pivots (Table 3) can be called an ablation study ( which is the only ablation study in this work). 
* In Fig 4 and Fig5, authors should give clear description of each column. For example, Pivot1 should be MAGA(pivot1). Otherwise, the "Pivot" column may be regarded as pivot images.
* Another issue is that the evluation dataset seems too simple (expecially dSprites). In 3D shapes dataset, the performace promotion is limited (far from solved).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The proposed method is clear but the evaluation experiments are far from enough.
content.summary_of_the_review: In conclusion, this work propose a new architecture to model differences between image pairs. To be honest, it is not a very new idea to model differences. Meanwhile, the fatal drawback of this work is th lacking of enough experiment to prove the rationality of model design.

content.title: MAGA: Modeling a Group Action
content.TL;DR: We make a new generative model that is capable of combinatorial generalization.
content.abstract:
Combinatorial generalization, an ability to collect various attributes from diverse data and assemble them to generate novel unexperienced data, is considered an essential traversal point to achieve human-level intelligence.
Previous unsupervised approaches mainly focused on  learning the disentangled representation, such as the variational autoencoder. However, recent studies discovered that the disentangled representation is insufficient for combinatorial generalization and is not even correlated. In this regard, we proposed a novel framework of data generation that can robustly generalize under these distribution shift situations. The model, simulating the group action, carries out combinatorial generalization by discovering the fundamental transformation between the data. We conducted experiments on the two settings: Recombination-to-Element, and Recombination-to-Range. The experiments demonstrated that our method has quantitatively and qualitatively superior generalizability and generates better images over traditional models.
